{{Short description|Pairing in algebra between ext groups of modules}}
In algebra, the '''Yoneda product''' (named after [[Nobuo Yoneda]]) is the [[pairing]] between [[Ext group]]s of [[module (mathematics)|modules]]:
<math display="block">\operatorname{Ext}^n(M, N) \otimes \operatorname{Ext}^m(L, M) \to \operatorname{Ext}^{n+m}(L, N)</math>
induced by
<math display="block">\operatorname{Hom}(N, M) \otimes \operatorname{Hom}(M, L) \to \operatorname{Hom}(N, L),\, f \otimes g \mapsto g \circ f.</math>

Specifically, for an element <math>\xi \in \operatorname{Ext}^n(M, N) </math>, thought of as an extension 
<math display="block">\xi :  0 \rightarrow N \rightarrow E_0 \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow E_{n-1} \rightarrow M \rightarrow 0 , </math>
and similarly 
<math display="block">\rho : 0 \rightarrow M \rightarrow F_0\rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow F_{m-1} \rightarrow L \rightarrow 0 \in \operatorname{Ext}^m(L, M),</math>
we form the Yoneda (cup) product 
<math display="block">\xi \smile \rho : 0 \rightarrow N \rightarrow E_0 \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow E_{n-1} \rightarrow F_0 \rightarrow \cdots \rightarrow F_{m-1} \rightarrow L \rightarrow 0 \in \operatorname{Ext}^{m + n}(L, N).</math>

Note that the middle map <math>E_{n-1} \rightarrow F_0</math> factors through the given maps to <math>M</math>.

We extend this definition to include <math>m, n = 0</math> using the usual [[functor]]iality of the <math>\operatorname{Ext}^*(\cdot,\cdot)</math> groups.

== Applications ==

=== Ext Algebras ===
Given a [[commutative ring]] <math>R</math> and a module <math>M</math>, the Yoneda product defines a product structure on the groups <math>\text{Ext}^\bullet(M,M)</math>, where <math>\text{Ext}^0(M,M) = \text{Hom}_R(M,M)</math> is generally a non-commutative ring. This can be generalized to the case of sheaves of modules over a [[ringed space]], or ringed topos.

=== Grothendieck duality ===
In Grothendieck's duality theory of coherent sheaves on a projective scheme <math>i:X \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^n_k</math> of pure dimension <math>r</math> over an algebraically closed field <math>k</math>, there is a pairing <math display="block">\text{Ext}^p_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{O}_X, \mathcal{F}) \times
\text{Ext}^{r-p}_{\mathcal{O}_X}(\mathcal{F},\omega_X^\bullet) \to k</math> where <math>\omega_X</math> is the dualizing complex <math>\omega_X = \mathcal{Ext}_{\mathcal{O}_\mathbb{P}}^{n-r}(i_*\mathcal{F},\omega_{\mathbb{P}})</math> and <math>\omega_{\mathbb{P}} = \mathcal{O}_\mathbb{P}(-(n+1))</math> given by the Yoneda pairing.<ref>{{Cite book | last1=Altman|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/BFb0060932 |title=Grothendieck Duality |last2=Kleiman |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|year=1970|volume=146 | isbn=978-3-540-04935-7 |pages=5 | doi=10.1007/BFb0060932}}</ref>

=== Deformation theory ===
The Yoneda product is useful for understanding the obstructions to a [[Deformation theory|deformation of maps]] of [[Ringed topos|ringed topoi]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://sites.mathdoc.fr/PMO/PDF/I_ILLUSIE-64.pdf | title=Complexe cotangent; application a la theorie des deformations | last=Illusie | first=Luc |author-link=Luc Illusie | page=163}}</ref> For example, given a composition of ringed topoi <math display="block">X \xrightarrow{f} Y \to S</math> and an <math>S</math>-extension <math>j:Y \to Y'</math> of <math>Y</math> by an <math>\mathcal{O}_Y</math>-module <math>J</math>, there is an obstruction class <math display="block">\omega(f,j) \in \text{Ext}^2(\mathbf{L}_{X/Y}, f^*J)</math> which can be described as the yoneda product <math display="block">\omega(f,j) = f^*(e(j))\cdot K(X/Y/S)</math>
where
<math display="block">\begin{align}
K(X/Y/S) &\in \text{Ext}^1(\mathbf{L}_{X/Y}, \mathbf{L}_{Y/S}) \\
f^*(e(j)) &\in \text{Ext}^1(f^*\mathbf{L}_{Y/S}, f^*J) 
\end{align}</math> and <math>\mathbf{L}_{X/Y}</math> corresponds to the [[cotangent complex]].
